* WHERE...Coastal Del Norte, Northern Coastal Humboldt,

* WHEN...Until 10 PM PST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous surf conditions and localized beach

properties.instruction:

run-up on beaches with waves topping and washing over large rocks
and jetties. These large waves can be erratic and unpredictable.

capable of sweeping people into the frigid and turbulent ocean
water. Mariners traversing the bar are urged to exercise extreme
caution or stay in port until the threat subsides. Please contact
the U.S. Coast Guard for information regarding harbor and bar
closures.

properties.areaDesc: San Luis Obispo County Beaches; Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 16 at 2:35PM PST until November 18 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 12 to
18 feet lowering to 8 to 12 feet on Wednesday. For the Coastal
Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 4 AM PST Wednesday.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 9 PM PST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths,
and harbor walkways. Moderate beach erosion is likely.
Isolated damage is unlikely but possible. There is an
increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull
swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can
cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize
small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The High Surf Advisory will need to be
extended beyond Wednesday and possibly through the week, with a
moderate chance of a High Surf Warning on Thursday.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow expected. Total snow accumulations between 10 and

gusting as high as 35 mph.

* WHERE...The Winter Storm Warning is for areas above 4000 ft,
including Snowman and Dead Horse Summits on highway 89, and Everitt

Weed, and the cities of Mount Shasta City and McCloud.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult to impossible. The
hazardous conditions will impact the Wednesday morning and evening
commutes. Gusty winds could bring down tree branches. Roads, and
especially bridges and overpasses, will likely become slick and
hazardous. The strong winds and weight of snow on tree limbs may
down power lines and could cause sporadic power outages.
properties.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. The latest road conditions
for the state you are calling from can be obtained by calling 5 1 1.

Persons should delay all travel if possible. If travel is absolutely
necessary, drive with extreme caution and be prepared for sudden
changes in visibility. Leave plenty of room between you and the
motorist ahead of you, and allow extra time to reach your
destination. Avoid sudden braking or acceleration, and be especially
cautious on hills or when making turns. Make sure your car is
winterized and in good working order.
